question: Does the strict positive +1.57pp worst-case empirical FV-minus-FIII initiation bound remain positive after sampling uncertainty within sites or replacement of the six observed projects?
original_label_assumption: 422 initiators and 53 day90-supported negatives are fixed; 100 short-followup negatives independently may be latent starts. Existing bounds are sharp for the observed finite sample under these assumptions.

method.rng: xorshift32; convert unsigned uint32 to U[0,1) by /2^32
method.within_project_fish: Resample exactly n categorical observations (source classified start, short-followup classified negative, day90-supported negative) WITH replacement in every project×stage (FIII and FV), preserving project×stage n. Recompute the pooled FV−FIII lower and upper sharp bounds using original fixed denominator N; keep six projects fixed.
method.project_cluster: Resample six projects with replacement as complete observed project×stage count tables; recompute pooled lower/upper bounds, and equal-project mean interval. No independent-fish resampling in this variant.
outputs: bootstrap 2.5%/97.5% lower-bound and upper-bound endpoint ranges
fraction of bootstrap draws with FV-minus-FIII lower bound strictly positive

inference_limits: Original sharp bound is logical finite-sample identification conditional on allowed relabelings, not a confidence interval.
Fish-within-project resampling assumes exchangeable independent animals within each stage×project, and does not incorporate tag dependence, measurement error, or full sampling frame.
Project bootstrap has only six heterogeneous clusters; its percentiles are descriptive stability diagnostics not rigorous population-level confidence intervals.
Neither procedure identifies true initiation probabilities or causal physiological silvering effects.
If a resampled strict lower bound is negative, that is evidence the positive empirical bound is sampling-sensitive; not proof of negative stage effects.
